target_customer: C-suite technology executives (mostly CIOs) as the community, and technology vendors who pay for insight, content and marketing intelligence
problem: IT executives relied on analyst firms and echo chambers for buying decisions. Pulse crowdsourced verified executive opinions through short questions so they could learn directly from each other.
business_model: B2B marketplace and research platform; vendors pay for insight and product recommendation tools

competitors.name: Gartner Peer Insights
competitors.what: Peer review platform for enterprise software by the incumbent analyst firm

technical_complexity.rationale: A verified community, polling and analytics product; the hard part was recruiting executives, not engineering.

defensibility.rationale: A verified C suite community and accumulated survey data are hard to replicate quickly, but review sites such as G2, TrustRadius and Gartner Peer Insights competed for the same vendor budgets.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Gartner bought Pulse in June 2021 and folded it into its Peer Insights platform.

market_need_then: Executives wanted peer input on technology purchases instead of analyst reports; Pulse reported nearly 15,000 C suite members and named Salesforce, Microsoft, Okta and Dialpad as customers on its YC page.

branding.domain_note: Used pulse.qa, a country code domain, because the exact pulse.com was not theirs; the company later appeared as Pulse Q&A.

identity.voice_and_tone: Crowdsourced Gartner framing aimed at CIOs

branding.community_and_virality: Built around a verified CIO community. Searches for brand press returned mostly unrelated companies called Pulse.

brand_strength.rationale: A generic name with a distinct niche community; search results show heavy collision with other Pulse companies.

outcome_analysis: Pulse raised a 4 million dollar seed after YC Winter 2018 and a 6.5 million Series A in 2020 around a verified community of executives, positioned against analyst firms. Gartner acquired it in June 2021 to fold into Peer Insights, a modest strategic exit by an incumbent rather than a venture scale outcome. The price is not confirmed.
